judgments.a_csv_targets: Justified. The official README (2024-09-16) says the CSVs are decoded-model metrics computed with the original 3DGS code and fix the earlier W&B numbers that omitted quantization/compression loss (and Dr Johnson attribution); sizes agree with the paper (40.28 vs 40.3 MB). They are the right reference for an eval-on-decoded-model reproduction. Caveats: v2 Table 1 (27.64) is pre-fix and stays the published claim, so report both; CSV came from black-background 3DGS-code rendering, so compare improvements over our own baseline rather than absolute PSNR.
judgments.b_codec_env: Equivalent. Official environment.yml pins imagecodecs[all]==2023.9.18 with numpy<2 on py3.10; the target dir holds the same wheel (bundled libjxl 0.8.2, confirmed by probe evidence) and the worker calls imagecodecs.imwrite(file, array, level=level) exactly as compression/jpeg_xl.py, with default effort/distance, float32 C-contiguous arrays passed via lossless np.save/np.load. Quantize/normalize numerics run in numpy 2.2.6 in-process; I checked float32 scalar promotion (python float/int vs np.float32) gives the same float32 results as numpy 1.26 with pandas float64 scalars.

summary: No critical or major issues found. Pruning, PLAS keys/normalization/schedule, joint permutation, smoothness loss, log-xyz split, densification config, bit depths, JXL levels, decode replacement and size computation all match the official code @5f2b360. Remaining risk is only unexercised full-scale (30000-step) behaviour and shared runtime gaps.
